_schema.description: Standards for writing plan-stage documents in Forms Portal — Feature Specifications (spec.md), Implementation Plans (plan.md), and Architecture Notes (ideas/arch_*.md). These are documents whose primary voice is 'what we WILL build', not 'what IS shipped'. AI agents MUST follow these rules when writing or editing any of these three document types.

companion_standards.readme_standards_shipped: .specify/memory/standards/readme_standards_shipped.json — for Module READMEs documenting already-shipped code
companion_standards.constitution: .specify/memory/constitution.md — project principles and governance (Principle VII: Documentation Lifecycle)

_usage._note_to_agent: READ THIS BLOCK FIRST. It tells you whether this file applies to the document you are about to write or edit.
applies_to: Feature Specification: .specify/specs/[###-feature-name]/spec.md — what + why, no implementation detail
Architecture Note: ideas/arch_*.md — cross-cutting decisions affecting multiple features
use_when: Writing a new Feature Specification for unimplemented work via /speckit-specify
Writing a new Implementation Plan via /speckit-plan
Writing an Architecture Note for a cross-cutting design decision (ideas/arch_*.md)
Updating any of the above while work is actively in progress
Writing any document whose primary voice is 'what we WILL build' rather than 'what IS shipped'
do_not_use_when: Writing a Module README for code that is ALREADY RUNNING — use .specify/memory/standards/readme_standards_shipped.json instead. Module READMEs have a stricter lifecycle: maintenance contract, mermaid rules, Quick Reference Card.
Writing a tasks.md file — that is generated by /speckit-tasks and follows its own format
A plan that has been fully implemented — freeze the plan and create a Module README per readme_standards_shipped.json for the shipped code
_usage.core_distinction_from_shipped: A plan-stage document is a TIME-BOUNDED DESIGN ARTIFACT. It describes intent, not reality. When the work ships, the plan is frozen — no one rewrites history on it. A Module README is a LIVING DOCUMENT that must stay in sync with code forever. Mixing these two voices in one file is how stale-doc bugs are born.
_usage.why_this_file_exists: spec-kit provides templates for spec.md and plan.md. What templates do NOT enforce is writing quality: future-tense voice, no mermaid of unshipped code, correct lifecycle stages, useful trade-offs sections. This file is the quality rulebook for all plan-stage documents.
lifecycle: 1. DRAFT — writing the spec or plan; doc lives in .specify/specs/[###-feature-name]/; heavily edited
2. IN_PROGRESS — /speckit-tasks has created tasks.md; phases executing; doc header says 'Status: In progress'
3. IMPLEMENTED — all tasks in tasks.md complete; doc header says 'Status: Implemented — all N tasks complete'. Doc is FROZEN at this point.
4. HISTORICAL — new work refers back to the frozen plan via links. Never rewritten. If follow-up work is needed, create a NEW spec.

readme_header.description: Every plan-stage document must have a consistent header block at the top.
required_fields: # <Document Title>   (H1 — document title, one per file. Use spec-kit titles: 'Feature Specification', 'Implementation Plan', or 'Architecture Note')
## <Subtitle — the feature or system being designed>
**Spec:** link to spec.md (for plan.md only — omit in spec.md itself and arch_*.md)
**Status:** Draft | In progress | Implemented | Frozen — required on ALL plan-stage docs; absent from Module READMEs
rules: The H1 title is the only H1 in the entire file
All major sections use H2 (##); subsections use H3 (###)
**Status** field is REQUIRED for all plan-stage docs

Once Status=Implemented, DO NOT edit the doc except to: (a) correct the Status line, (b) add the tasks.md completion reference, (c) fix factual errors that predate ship. No retroactive design changes.
Include an 'Agent note' callout immediately after the header block citing the applicable standards file: .specify/memory/standards/readme_standards_plan.json
example: ## Field authoring, section management, and branching logic for Forms Portal
> **Agent note:** This is a plan-stage document. When editing, follow `.specify/memory/standards/readme_standards_plan.json`.
> For Module READMEs documenting shipped code, use `.specify/memory/standards/readme_standards_shipped.json`.

index_section.description: Every plan-stage document must have an Index section immediately after the header block.
index_section.position: First section after the opening --- divider
index_section.heading: ## Index
index_section.format: Markdown table with columns: # | Section | Summary
rules: Plan-stage docs do NOT have a Quick Reference Card — that is a Module README feature. Docs open directly into Section 1.
Row numbers match the order sections appear in the document
Each row links to the section anchor using markdown link syntax: [Label](#anchor)
Anchor format: GitHub Flavored Markdown (lowercase, spaces to hyphens, remove non-alphanumeric except hyphens)
Summary column: one concise line per row — no full paragraphs

required_sections.description: Advisory section guidance — NOT a competing structure with the spec-kit template. These tell you WHAT TO COVER within the template's sections. Any section irrelevant to the specific feature may be omitted. Voice must remain 'what we WILL build' throughout.

sections.heading: Why We Need This
sections.content: What pain point or gap are we solving? What exists today and why is it insufficient? Concrete examples of the current state. NO solution here — just the problem.

sections.heading: Current State (if extending existing code)
sections.content: Audit of what is already in place. Models, services, relevant views, known bugs. The reader should finish this section knowing exactly what they are about to replace or extend. Omit for net-new features with no prior art.

sections.heading: Proposed Design
sections.content: The new design. Use a comparison table (Aspect | Current | Proposed) for every dimension that is changing. Explain the WHY for each decision.

sections.heading: Design Principles
sections.content: Short numbered list of the invariants the design must satisfy. These are the things reviewers will hold the implementation to.

sections.heading: Architecture Sketch
sections.content: High-level picture. ASCII diagrams preferred — mermaid labels for unshipped code will drift the moment code is written. See no_mermaid_of_unshipped_code rules.

sections.heading: Phases
sections.content: Phase-by-phase breakdown. Each phase should be a deployable unit. Reference tasks.md as the SSOT for task status — do not duplicate task lists here. See task_tracking_ssot rules.

sections.heading: Trade-offs Considered
sections.content: What other designs were considered and why were they rejected? This is the most important section for future developers — it prevents re-litigating decisions months later.

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.content: Unresolved decisions. Mark each with the person who needs to decide and a target date. Delete items as they are resolved. Should be empty or near-empty by Status=Implemented.

sections.heading: Related Files
sections.content: Table of existing code touched by this design + other spec/plan docs + companion files. Columns: File | Role in this feature.

sections.heading: Version History
sections.content: Version history of this DOCUMENT — how the design evolved during discussion, not how the code evolved. Table: Version | Date | Change | Decided by.

version_history_rules.description: Rules for the document's own version history — tracking how the DESIGN evolved, not how the CODE evolved.
rules: Add a new row at the TOP for every significant design change during Draft and In_progress phases
Version format: major.minor — increment MAJOR when the design changes meaningfully, MINOR for wording/section additions
Date format: YYYY-MM-DD
Description: state WHAT changed in the design and WHY the team made that call. Include 'Decided by' so future developers know who to ask.
Once Status=Implemented, STOP adding rows. The document is frozen.
If follow-up work is needed after ship, create a NEW spec — do not re-open an implemented one.
version_history_rules.example_row: | 1.2 | 2026-05-20 | Changed branching model from multi-condition (AND/OR) to single-condition only for v1 — AND/OR complexity deferred to v2. Decided by: Domain Expert + AI session 2026-05-20. |

task_tracking_ssot.description: tasks.md (created by /speckit-tasks) is the Single Source of Truth for task status. Plan-stage documents MUST reference it, not duplicate it.
rules: Once /speckit-tasks has created tasks.md, that file is the SSOT for all task status — not the plan doc
A Phases section in the plan lists phase goals and deliverables — NOT individual task status or completion checkboxes
Never manually update task status in a plan doc — update tasks.md via /speckit-implement or directly
If a reader needs to know what tasks are remaining, point them to tasks.md — do not maintain a parallel list in the plan
Reference tasks.md in the plan's Related Files section: 'tasks.md | Active task list (SSOT for task status)'
phase_section_format: > **Task status**: See `tasks.md` Phase 1 section — that file is the SSOT.
**Goal**: [What is deployable and testable at the end of this phase]
**Key decisions**: [Design choices that apply only to this phase]
**Acceptance criteria**: [How we know this phase is complete]

rules: H1 (#): Document title only — exactly ONE per file
H2 (##): Major sections — typically numbered in plans (## 1. Why We Need This, ## 2. Current State)
H3 (###): Subsections
H4 (####): Only if a subsection itself needs sub-grouping — use sparingly
Never skip levels

anchor_generation.description: How GitHub Flavored Markdown generates anchor IDs from headings — used for Index links.
algorithm: 1. Take the heading text (exclude the # prefix)
3. Remove characters that are not letters, digits, spaces, or hyphens

writing_style.description: Writing style rules for plan-stage documents.
rules: Use FUTURE TENSE and conditional mood — 'we will add X', 'the system will support Y', 'the goal is to...'. This is the core voice difference from Module READMEs.
Use tables over bullet lists for structured data (current vs proposed, trade-offs, phases)
Use numbered lists for sequential phases and steps
Use blockquotes (>) for critical design principles that should not drift
Bold (**text**) for: principle names, column headers, 'DECIDED:' / 'OPEN:' markers in open questions
Code blocks for illustrative code sketches — clearly label as 'sketch' or 'proposed interface'
Avoid over-committing to implementation detail — leave room for the implementer to make small decisions
Section summaries in the Index must be ONE concise line

no_mermaid_of_unshipped_code.description: Plan-stage documents MUST NOT contain mermaid diagrams of code that does not exist yet. This is the strongest rule in this file.
why: Mermaid labels are specific — function names, field names, model classes. When the implementer ships the code, those names WILL change from the plan sketch. The diagram becomes wrong on day 1.
Readers trust diagrams more than prose. A wrong diagram is worse than no diagram.
If you need a visual, use an ASCII sketch clearly marked 'PROPOSED — not yet implemented, names may change'. ASCII signals rough intent in a way mermaid does not.
allowed_mermaid_uses_in_plans: Diagrams showing the CURRENT state drawn from existing, already-running code the plan is replacing
Very high-level conceptual diagrams with no function names or model fields — pure abstraction (e.g., user roles, data flow stages). These survive the draft-to-implementation transition.
Diagrams that will be LIFTED into the Module README once work completes. Delete the copy in the plan when Status=Implemented so there is only one source of truth.
forbidden_mermaid_uses_in_plans: Diagrams of functions, classes, or models that do not exist yet
Diagrams with specific field names, DB table names, or method signatures — those are implementation decisions that have not happened yet
Diagrams that claim to show 'the architecture' of unwritten code

freezing_a_plan.description: The process to follow when a plan-stage document has been fully implemented.
steps: 1. Update Status field in header from 'In progress' to 'Implemented — all N tasks complete'
2. Verify tasks.md shows all tasks complete

3. Verify every 'we will' / 'the plan is to' sentence reflects what was intended. If decisions changed during implementation, leave the plan UNCHANGED — the plan records original intent; the Module README is the source of truth for what is actually running.
4. Move any 'Open Questions' items to: (a) Closed status in the plan, or (b) a new spec if they represent follow-up work
5. Add a final row to Version History: 'vN.M | YYYY-MM-DD | Plan frozen — work complete. See Module README for current shipped behavior.'
6. Add a link in Related Files pointing to the Module README of the landing app, so a reader of the frozen plan can find the authoritative current state
7. Do NOT delete the plan — it remains the record of design intent and trade-offs considered
